title: Pin + Rollout Interaction: region-aware tier routing and fallback model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a clear product and implementation specification for how model version pinning interacts with smart routing policies (region selection, tier routing) and rollout strategies (canary/A-B). This ticket codifies expected behavior, API contract changes, admin/console UX, and failure/fallback semantics for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Background / why this matters:
- Customers can pin production services to specific model versions for compliance or quality stability. At the same time they expect smart routing (route by region, customer tier, or cost policy) and rollouts (canary/A-B) to operate as a single predictable system.
- Current behavior is underspecified: pins are sometimes overridden by fallback routing rules during capacity constraints, and canary cohorts may see inconsistent model versions across regions. This causes customer confusion and intermittent regressions.

Goals:
1) Define deterministic precedence and resolution rules when pins, routing policies, and rollouts conflict.
2) Specify API/console surface for pinning scope (route-level, org-level, region-scoped) and how rollouts reference pinned baseline/variants.
3) Ensure reliable fallback semantics that never violate pin constraints unless explicitly allowed by an escape hatch.
4) Provide telemetry and rollout observability (per-cohort model exposure, errors, SLO drift).

Proposed high-level rules (product-first):
- Strong pin: If a customer sets a "strong" pin on a route or org to a specific model:version, all routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, and canary/A-B assignment) must respect that pinned model; routing can only change selected instance endpoints but not the model artifact.
- Scope: Pins are scoped at three levels: route-level > project/org-level > account-level. More specific scope overrides less specific.
- Canary/A-B composition: Rollouts operate by assigning traffic cohorts to model variants. If a strong pin exists for the route/org, canary cohorts must be created only among versions that are compatible with the pin (e.g., same major version or a validated upgrade path). If the pin disallows the candidate variant, the rollout fails validation.
- Fallbacks: Fallback model variants (used when capacity or regional availability prevents the primary model) may be used only if the pin explicitly lists fallback variants or if an "allow-fallback" flag is enabled at the route level. By default, fallback to non-pinned models is forbidden.
- Region selection: Routing by region should select endpoints that host the pinned model. If the pinned model is not available in the preferred region, behavior depends on pin policy:
   * fail-fast: return a capacity/unavailable error
   * cross-region failover: route to another region that has the pinned model (if customer enabled cross-region failover)
- Tier routing: Customer tiers that map to model classes (e.g., premium -> high-capacity model) must be compatible with pin scope; if a pin forces a lower-capacity model into a premium tier, show a console warning and require explicit confirmation.

API & Console changes (summary):
- Pin object model (POST/PUT /pins): scope, model:version, mode=[strong|soft], allowed_fallbacks=[], allow_cross_region_failover=[true|false], description
- Rollout object (POST/PUT /rollouts): cohort definition, variants[], validation_rules (compatibility checks against active pins), abort_on_pin_violation=[true|false]
- Console UX: route-level pin editor, rollout preview with "pin compatibility" validation, per-region availability hints, and a warning when tier routing conflicts with pins.

Acceptance criteria (see list below):
- API accepts pin creation requests and enforces validation rules.
- Console surfaces pin scope and warns on conflicts.
- Rollouts cannot launch if they propose variants incompatible with strong pins.
- Fallbacks to non-pinned models are blocked unless allow_fallback explicit.
- Telemetry logs model_version exposure per-request, per-region, and per-cohort for at least 30 days.

Edge cases & trade-offs:
- Backward compatibility: Existing pinned customers default to strong semantics to avoid silent breakage. This may reduce availability during outages; provide opt-in to soft pins to preserve availability.
- Operational complexity: Enforcing pins at routing layer constrains capacity-based autoscaling and cross-region fallbacks. Trade-off between strict correctness (respect pin) and availability (allow fallback).
- Private deployments: For VPC/on-prem, customers might run different model catalogs per region. Pin enforcement must be evaluated against the deployment's local catalog (no cross-region failover allowed by default).

Telemetry & success metrics:
- <metric:pin-respected-rate> percentage of requests that honored route pin when it existed (target: 99.9%)
- <metric:rollout-validation-failures> number of rollouts blocked due to pin incompatibility (investigate causes)
- SLO: no customer-facing increase in model-mismatch errors during rollout (target: zero regressions for pinned routes)

Implementation notes for ENG:
- Routing decision sequence: (1) Evaluate strong pin scope and resolve allowed model set. (2) Apply rollout assignment (cohort -> variant) constrained to allowed set. (3) Apply region/tier routing to select endpoint hosting the chosen variant; if not available, consult fallback policy.
- Cache behavior: pinned routes should bypass or consult prefix/KV cache policies carefully; ensure cached responses are tagged with model_version to prevent serving stale outputs after rollouts.
- Data model: pin must be a first-class entity in control plane with versioned history and audit logs (PRD link below).

Links / artifacts:
- PRD draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/pinning-rollouts-PRD (placeholder)
- Console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/mockups/pin-rollout-2026-02
- Engineering spike notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/1283
- SRE runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Pinning-Fallbacks

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- PM: finalize wording for pin modes and default behavior (Aisha)
- ENG: spike to surface model availability per-region within routing layer (Marco) - target spike 1 week
- Design: produce lightweight UX for pin editor and rollout compatibility preview (Diane)
acceptance_criteria: API allows creation of pinned objects with scope and mode and rejects incompatible rollouts
Console shows pin scope on route pages and warns on conflicts with tier routing
Rollouts validate candidate variants against active strong pins and block if incompatible
Fallbacks to non-pinned models are only allowed when allow_fallback=true on the pin
Telemetry emits per-request model_version and cohort metadata for 30 days
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Initial drafting complete. Shared with ENG and Design for feedback.
2026-02-24 Marco Li: ENG spike started. Need an API hook in routing decision path to resolve pin before cohort assignment. Blocking item: infra needs a per-region model catalog API (ENG-3717).
2026-03-02 Diane Park (Design): Mockups uploaded. UX suggestion: show "compatibility score" in rollout preview (0-100) and highlight incompatible changes.
2026-03-07 Rajesh Singh (SRE): Concern about strict strong pins causing cross-region blackholes during outages. Propose a soft-fallback policy with automatic alerting and opt-in failover.

2026-03-10 Marco Li: Updated API proposal in PR #1283. Implementation plan: routing will evaluate pin first, then cohort assignment. See GH PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/1283
notes: We must align naming: 'strong' vs 'soft' pin instead of 'hard' to avoid legal connotations.
Privacy: pins and rollouts must be logged for audit with user id and timestamp. For Private deployments ensure logs respect retention policies.
